candidates.title: Beyond positive thinking: A randomized trial of mental contrasting with implementation intentions to curb academic procrastination
candidates.review_notes: High-priority lead for reviewing WOOP/MCII and task-initiation content. The reported randomized study is small and limited to undergraduates at one private Chinese university, so it must not justify broad population claims or a universal anti-procrastination protocol.

candidates.title: The association between sleep variability and cognitive function: A systematic review and meta analysis
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision sleep-variability-cognition-2026 reviewed the publisher source and keeps this as watch: greater sleep variability is associated with poorer cognition on average, but the evidence does not justify a causal sleep-regularity protocol or fixed schedule prescription.

candidates.title: Should we all just take 10? A meta-analysis of wakeful rest
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision wakeful-rest-memory-2026 supports a conservative post-learning quiet-rest experiment. The source reports substantial heterogeneity and weaker effects in healthy young to middle-aged adults, so Brali does not publish a universal ten-minute dose or guaranteed memory benefit.

candidates.title: Research on the testing effect routinely conflates direct and forward testing effects: A meta-analysis of testing effects with free recall
candidates.container_title: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision testing-effect-direct-forward-2026 challenges undifferentiated testing-effect language. The meta-analysis separates direct memory benefits for tested material from forward effects on subsequently learned material and finds that most included effects came from mixed designs.

candidates.title: Mixed effects of retrieval practice on the acquisition of procedural knowledge in verb spelling education
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision retrieval-procedural-application-2026 challenges the assumption that better rule retention means better application. In this classroom study, retrieval plus worked examples improved rule retention after one week but not rule application compared with worked examples alone.

candidates.title: Acute cognitive effects of interruptions to prolonged sitting with brief standing or physical activity breaks: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
candidates.container_title: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision movement-breaks-cognition-2026 reviewed the source and keeps this as watch: the meta-analysis reports small acute executive/memory effects but mostly low or very-low certainty and does not justify a cognitive-optimization break interval, duration, or intensity prescription.
